mainEntity.name: Does this account for muscle mass?

acceptedAnswer.text: No — like standard BMI, this range doesn't distinguish between muscle and fat, so very muscular individuals may fall above this range while still being at a healthy body composition.

mainEntity.name: Should I try to hit the exact middle of this range?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily — this range is a general statistical reference, not a personalized target. Where you sit within (or even slightly outside) this range depends on individual factors like frame size and muscle mass.

mainEntity.name: Why is there a lower range for some ethnic backgrounds?

acceptedAnswer.text: Research shows people from South Asian, Chinese, other Asian, Middle Eastern, Black African and African-Caribbean backgrounds tend to develop weight-related conditions such as type 2 diabetes at a lower BMI, so NICE recommends treating a BMI of 23 as the start of overweight for these groups.
